report:
The unrestricted P03 completion criteria are not met. Independent reconstruction establishes the restricted statements A–F and their supplied proofs; I found no concrete mathematical defect in them. The constant-minimum hypothesis is an explicit antecedent, and no argument establishes it, or supplies another positive-current construction, for arbitrary compact strictly LCK manifolds. Both explicit families have pseudoeffective Lee-curvature classes, so neither is a counterexample.

For A–B, local exactness λ=df gives λᶜ=dᶜf and κ=−ddᶜf, establishing reality, type (1,1), closedness and de Rham exactness with precisely the stipulated normalization. Conformal change gives λ′=λ+da and κ′=κ−ddᶜa. Writing Q=λ∧λᶜ=(i/(2π))λ¹⁰∧λ⁰¹ shows that Q is semipositive and nonzero wherever λ is nonzero. Nonexactness ensures a nonempty open set of such points. Direct differentiation, including the degree-one sign, gives
 d(λᶜ∧κ^(k−1)∧ω^(n−k))=−κ^k∧ω^(n−k)+(n−k)Q∧κ^(k−1)∧ω^(n−k).
Compact Stokes therefore proves every asserted identity for 1≤k≤n. The cases k=1 and k=n give the strictly positive first integral and zero top integral. Here n≥2 is essential to the first conclusion.

The nonzero ordinary Bott–Chern conclusion is also established, rather than inferred from de Rham exactness. If κ=ddᶜa globally, e^aω has zero Lee curvature and still has nonexact Lee form λ+da. Applying the same k=1 identity to that metric contradicts its zero left side and strictly positive right side.

For the volume ray, dη_t=λ∧ω, and Stokes gives ∫κ∧η_t^(n−1)=(n−1)∫Q∧ω∧η_t^(n−2). Consequently V′(t)=n(n−1)∫Q∧ω∧η_t^(n−2), strictly positive whenever η_t is positive. The coefficient of t^n is ∫κ^n=0. These calculations require no Gauduchon condition and use ordinary wedge powers throughout.

For C, let the constant least relative eigenvalue be r. If r<0, then η_t is positive for 0≤t<−1/r, while η_(−1/r) is semipositive with a kernel at every point. Its top power therefore vanishes everywhere. This contradicts monotonicity and continuity of V, which give V(−1/r)≥V(0)>0. Thus κ is semipositive. Its nonnegative continuous top power has zero integral, hence vanishes identically; the least eigenvalue is consequently zero everywhere. The previously proved nonzero Bott–Chern class has κ itself as a closed positive-current representative. Wedge positivity gives nonnegative pairing against every positive Gauduchon test. No rank constancy was used. Under constant entire spectrum, the rank is constant, nonzero and at most n−1. On an actual compact quotient with invariant tensors, κ and ω have constant matrices in an invariant frame. Likewise, ddᶜγ^(n−1) is an invariant top form, hence a constant multiple of γ^n; Stokes forces that constant to vanish. This proves the invariant Gauduchon assertion without any lattice-existence or classification premise.

For D–E, scalar contraction acts freely and properly discontinuously: compact subsets of the punctured space have radii bounded above and away from zero, allowing only finitely many intersecting translates. A closed radial annulus supplies a compact fundamental set, and local quotient charts give the connected compact complex manifold. The bounds (1−ε)ρ≤Φ≤(1+ε)ρ ensure positivity. Both Φ and Ω scale by 1/4, so Ω/Φ and −d log Φ descend. Closedness of Ω gives the LCK equation, and a loop lifted from z to z/2 has Lee period 2 log 2, proving nonexactness.

The Hessian calculation is correct: relative curvature has matrix I−FF*/Φ, where F_i=bar(z_i)+εz_1δ_i1. Its spectrum is n−1 copies of 1 and h=1−|F|²/Φ. Substitution of z_1=x+iy gives exactly the stated formula for h, with range [−ε,ε]; at (1,0,…,0) the spectrum is −ε,1,…,1. The bounded smooth invariant correction u=log ρ−log Φ gives κ+ddᶜu=ddᶜ log ρ, whose Hessian is semipositive by Cauchy–Schwarz. Thus the negative eigenvalue does not disprove class pseudoeffectivity. At the first positive-ray boundary t=1/ε, the volume density relative to ω^n is (1+1/ε)^(n−1)(2(1−ε)y²+R)/Φ. It vanishes precisely on the stated real rays and is positive on an open set, so total volume remains positive. This explicitly verifies why pointwise first degeneration cannot replace the everywhere-degeneration step in C.

For F, differentiating f=q²/s with a=q/s gives f_(i bar j)=(2/s)(q_i−a s_i)(q_(bar j)−a s_(bar j))+2aδ_i1δ_j1−a²δ_ij. The first two terms are semipositive and 0≤a≤1, proving Ω_ε≥(1−ε)ddᶜs>0 for every stipulated ε. Homogeneity ensures descent, and division by s gives the asserted LCK equation and nonzero Lee period. Curvature is ddᶜ log s, semipositive of rank n−1, so its least relative eigenvalue is identically zero. At the first stated point, the Hessian of f is diag(1,−1,…,−1), giving spectrum 0,(1−ε)^(−1),…,(1−ε)^(−1). At the second point its Hessian vanishes, giving spectrum 0,1,…,1. This establishes genuine variation of the remaining spectrum in every n≥2.

These mathematical arguments are self-contained and invoke no nonroutine external theorem. The cited [primary paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.05595v2) was opened and confirms the historical Conjecture 5.13 context; its classification statements and Theorem 5.11 are not proof premises here. No Lamari-duality import is needed for the explicitly constructed smooth positive representatives. The only harmless terminology clarification is that ∫η_t^n equals n! times the usual metric volume; the draft’s stipulated convention leaves every identity and sign unchanged. Unrestricted P03 remains unresolved by this submission.
